reflections.title: "I Will Remember My Covenant"

reflect.text: A rainbow only appears when there are dark clouds and falling rain. Noah and his family endured a long, terrifying storm before they saw God's bow in the sky. In the same way, we often walk through prolonged seasons of sorrow or guilt before we see how God works for our good. When our conscience is clouded by past sin or heavy grief, Jesus is revealed to us like that heavenly rainbow, bringing peace and showing God's true mercy.

When clouds gather, faith looks beyond the storm to God's promise. His bow in the sky is turned upward toward heaven without an arrow or string, showing that He is no longer at war with us. Most comforting of all, God says that He will remember His covenant. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "it is God's remembering me which is the ground of my safety." Our hope does not depend on our frail memories, but on God, who never forgets His people.

questions: When dark clouds of sorrow or doubt gather in your life, what helps you look for God's promises instead of giving in to fear?
How does knowing that God's memory, rather than your own, keeps you safe bring peace to your heart today?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank you that you never forget your promises to us. When sorrow or guilt darkens our days, help us fix our eyes on Jesus and the peace He brings. Teach us to rest quietly in your unchanging love. Amen.

reflections.title: "Whenever the Rainbow Appears"

reflect.text: Violent storms remind us of nature's great power. For anyone who has lived through terrifying destruction, gathering storm clouds can trigger real fear and anxiety. God understands how easily our hearts are shaken, so He provided an active sign in the sky. The rainbow depicts a warrior's weapon hung up on the wall, showing that God has made a peaceful truce with creation.

God did not set the rainbow in the sky because He is in danger of forgetting His word. Instead, He gave this visible sign to comfort our anxious, doubtful hearts. Just as God later gave us baptism and the Lord's Supper as physical seals of His faithfulness, He gave the rainbow to assure us that His grace, love, and mercy will always outshine the darkest clouds.

questions: What fears or worries tend to make you feel anxious when life feels stormy?
How can physical reminders of God's promises, such as the rainbow or the Lord's Supper, help strengthen your faith?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank you for giving us visible signs of your peace and mercy. When our hearts are anxious and afraid, calm our thoughts with the truth of your Word. Help us trust that your grace is always stronger than any storm we face. Amen.

D4.author: Rev. Kyle Norman
D4.work: What Does the Rainbow Really Mean? - The Crosswalk Devotional - March 16

reflections.title: God's Covenant with Creation

reflect.text: Poets admire the rainbow for its beauty, and scientists can explain how sunlight bends through water drops. Yet poetry and science only explain how the rainbow looks and works. We need God's Word to show us what it truly means. In this passage, God reveals that this arch in the sky is His binding covenant, a sacred promise made to Noah, his family, and every living creature.

Natural wonders find their richest meaning when we view them through the truth of Scripture. The sky is not an empty canvas, but a reminder of the faithful Creator who preserves our earth. When we observe God's faithfulness displayed across creation, our hearts are drawn to respond with humble worship and deep thanksgiving.

questions: How does reading the Bible change the way you understand and appreciate the natural world around you?
What is one part of God's creation that moves you to thank Him for His daily care and faithfulness?
reflections.prayer: Gracious God, thank you for revealing the true meaning of your world through the Scriptures. Whenever we see the beauty of the earth and sky, remind us of your steady faithfulness. Fill our lives with genuine worship and gratitude for your enduring care. Amen.
